title: Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory, Part II: Lubin–Tate formal modules and quasi-canonical lifts
summary: Construct one-dimensional formal modules over the integers of finite extensions of Q_p, their logarithms, finite-height deformations and Lubin–Tate torsion characters. Compare with the existing arithmetic Artin map, prove the unramified Honda and supersingular elliptic comparison, and build marked quasi-canonical lattice quotients with their smallest quadratic ring-class fields. Both ramified and unramified CM extensions are included. The BKO specialization identifies tame and anticyclotomic towers and proves trace-compatible comparison maps.
readme:
# Lubin–Tate formal modules and quasi-canonical lifts

This is the formal-module continuation of **Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory**. It starts from that roadmap’s connected p-divisible groups, Tate modules and finite Dieudonné Frobenius. Its endpoints are the Lubin–Tate character comparison with the existing arithmetic Artin map, universal finite-height marked deformations, and the integral lattice construction of quasi-canonical lifts with their smallest marked ring-class fields. The BKO specialization constructs the two local towers and the maps between their formal traces.

The formal-module foundations apply to every finite extension K/Q_p. For the CM construction distinguish the coefficient field F0 from the CM extension F; the quadratic field-degree results cover both ramified and unramified F/F0, including residue characteristic two. Only the BKO and stated Honda comparison impose p≥5 and Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic. A higher-height cohomological tower theorem is not inferred from the rank-one Lubin–Tate character.

## Conventions

- O_K has uniformizer π and residue cardinality q. A formal O_K-module is one-dimensional, commutative, and has an actual unital O_K-action whose derivative is the coefficient structure map. Its O_K-height is h; the underlying p-divisible height is h[K:Q_p].
- A strict coordinate has derivative one. A marked deformation carries a specified identification of its special fiber; marked isomorphisms preserve that entire identification. These conditions are distinct.
- Formal logarithms have zero constant term and derivative one. Coordinate comparison includes the derivative factor. They converge on maximal ideals; their exponentials need only be inverse on a sufficiently deep ideal. Torsion prevents a general injectivity claim.
- Fix separable closures and embeddings before forming fields. Arithmetic reciprocity sends uniformizers to arithmetic Frobenius. Thus χ_π(Art_K(π^r u))=u^−1. Changing π to uπ twists χ by the unramified character with arithmetic Frobenius value u.
- The deformation coefficient ring B is specified with its residue field. No canonical Cohen ring for an arbitrary imperfect field is assumed. For finite k_F in the CM field problem choose B=O_(F^ur), where F^ur/F0 is the maximal unramified subextension of F/F0. This B embeds in every field whose marked modulus is considered.
- For a lattice L⊃T with [L:T]=q0^N, the quotient is marked to the q0^N-Frobenius twist. Multiplication by π_F supplies coherent comparison when that exponent changes by the residue degree. Over a nonclosed residue field one keeps the twist component rather than identifying forms after algebraic closure.
- For quadratic F/F0, O_s=O0+varpi0^s O_F uses the **smaller-field uniformizer**. Positive levels have degrees q0^(s−1)(q0+1) unramified and q0^s ramified. Canonical s=0 is separate. Minimal fields mean smallest fields **containing F for the marked deformation**; forgetting the marking or the CM coefficient field changes the question.
- In BKO, p≥5, Φ/Q_p is unramified quadratic and π=−p. Φ_n uses π^(n+1)-torsion, while Ψ′_s is the level-s quasi-canonical field. The comparison is Ψ_n=(Ψ′_(n+1))^Δ′, with |Δ′|=p+1. For [−p]v_(n+1)=v_n, the p-adic Tate generator is w_n=[(−1)^n]v_n.

## Existing inputs and boundaries

The existing Mathlib `FormalGroup` is the law carrier; commutativity is its separate `IsComm` class. `FormalGroup.map` is coefficient base change. `FormalGroup.Point` has power-series-valued parameters and does not supply maximal-ideal-valued points. Tau Ceti already supplies the Weierstrass law and its adic point group. For a height-one Dedekind adic-completion presentation it also supplies the unconditional `formalPointHomAdicCompletion`, its injectivity and its range. The generic `formalPointHom` has an explicit auxiliary-point hypothesis. Every comparison uses the applicable existing theorem with those hypotheses.

Formal CM does not imply global elliptic CM. |

## Library starting point

The input declarations below have been read at Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` and Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369`. In particular Weierstrass preparation and its quotient algebra equivalence already exist; the formal-module torsion construction uses them. The current roadmaps and current library have also been checked for existing ownership. The principal-unit logarithm is available in the current local-field development beyond these pins and is imported through LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1.

- **mathlib:FormalGroup** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean`): One-dimensional formal group law in two variables, with associativity and tangent identities; commutativity is the separate FormalGroup.IsComm class.
- **mathlib:FormalGroup.map** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean`): Coefficientwise base change of the existing law along a ring homomorphism.
- **mathlib:FormalGroup.Point** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/FormalGroup/Basic.lean`): Points in multivariate power series with nilpotent constant coefficient; these are not maximal-ideal-valued points of a valued field.
- **mathlib:PowerSeries.subst_substInvOfIsUnit_left** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Substitution.lean`): A zero-constant series with unit linear coefficient has a two-sided substitution inverse; the cited left identity and its adjacent right identity supply coordinate inverses.
- **mathlib:PowerSeries.eval₂Hom** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Evaluation.lean`): Evaluation as a ring homomorphism at a topologically nilpotent element of a complete separated linearly topologized ring, with continuous coefficient map.
- **mathlib:PowerSeries.comp_eval₂** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Evaluation.lean`): Evaluation commutes with a continuous ring homomorphism into another complete separated linear topological ring.
- **mathlib:PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassFactorization** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean`): Weierstrass factorization over a maximal-ideal-adically complete local ring when the reduced series is nonzero.
- **mathlib:PowerSeries.IsWeierstrassFactorizationAt.algEquivQuotient** (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean`): For a Weierstrass factorization, identifies the distinguished-polynomial quotient with the power-series quotient over an adically complete coefficient ring.
- **tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.formalGroup** (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Basic.lean`): The Weierstrass formal law on Mathlib FormalGroup, including the commutativity instance.
- **tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.map_formalGroup** (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Basic.lean`): The Weierstrass formal law commutes with coefficient base change.
- **tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.FormalGroupPoint** (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/AdicPoint.lean`): The newtype of parameters in an adic ideal, with evaluated elliptic addition, inverse and AddCommGroup structure.
- **tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.formalPointHom** (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Point/Hom.lean`): Injective formal parameter homomorphism into affine curve points, under the explicit auxiliary-point hypothesis haux; this is not an unconditional surjectivity theorem.
- **tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.formalPointHomAdicCompletion** (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Point/AdicCompletion.lean`): For a curve over the integers of a height-one Dedekind adic completion, elliptic over its completed fraction field, the formal parameter map is an unconditional additive homomorphism into affine points.
- **tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.formalPointHomAdicCompletion_injective** (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Point/AdicCompletion.lean`): The unconditional Dedekind adic-completion formal parameter homomorphism is injective.
- **tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.range_formalPointHomAdicCompletion** (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/FormalGroup/Point/Range.lean`): For that same Dedekind-completion presentation, its range is the identity together with points whose x-coordinate has valuation greater than one in the multiplicative convention; classically the kernel of reduction.

The layer descriptions state all endpoints and their domains. The full mathematical development, APIs, proof plans and discriminating examples are in the accompanying roadmap document.

stages.title: Formal modules, coordinates and complete points
stages.description:
Extend the native one-dimensional commutative formal law by actual homomorphisms and a tangent-compatible coefficient-ring action. Distinguish the library’s power-series-valued points from evaluated maximal-ideal points. Construct normalized logarithms and their deep analytic inverse, and compare the elliptic specialization to the existing law and point maps.

**Formal group homomorphisms.** For commutative rings R and commutative Mathlib formal laws F,G, a homomorphism is h∈XR[[X]] satisfying h(F(X,Y))=G(h(X),h(Y)). Hom(F,G) has pointwise G-addition; composition gives the endomorphism ring. An isomorphism has unit derivative and the existing substitution inverse; strict means derivative one. None of these conditions identifies the entire reduction with X.

**One-dimensional formal modules.** For a commutative ring A and A-algebra R, a one-dimensional formal A-module is a commutative Mathlib FormalGroup R and a unital ring homomorphism A→End_R(F) inducing the given A→R on derivatives. A-linear homs commute with every [a]. For A=O_K and a field k of residue characteristic, height h means the first nonzero term of [π] is cX^(q^h), c≠0; infinity means [π]=0. Heights of lifts are heights of their special fibers.

**Adic formal-module points.** Let R be a complete separated linearly topologized commutative A-algebra and I an ideal defining an adic topology. For a formal A-module over R, form the newtype F(I) of parameters in I, with evaluated formal addition, inverse and A-action. Continuous coefficient maps carrying I into J induce continuous A-linear maps. In particular F(m_L) exists for every complete finite extension L/K and F(m_Kbar) is the union over finite extensions, rather than an unjustified evaluation on an incomplete algebraic closure.

**Normalized formal logarithm.** For a commutative formal law F over a characteristic-zero domain R with fraction field K, construct the unique logarithm ℓ_F∈XK[[X]], ℓ′(0)=1, satisfying ℓ_F(F(X,Y))=ℓ_F(X)+ℓ_F(Y). Its inverse is the formal exponential. For h:F→G, ℓ_G∘h=h′(0)ℓ_F, and hence ℓ_F∘[a]=aℓ_F. These are formal identities; integral coefficients and convergence of the exponential on the whole maximal ideal are not asserted.

**Convergence of the formal logarithm.** For a formal group over the integers of a finite extension K/Q_p, its normalized logarithm converges on every m_L, L/K finite. It defines a homomorphism F(m_L)→L. There is a sufficiently deep power m_L^r on which log and exp are inverse analytic maps. Log is compatible with field embeddings, coordinate change and finite formal traces; no global injectivity on torsion is claimed.

stages.title: Lubin–Tate construction and coordinate independence
stages.description:
An admissible π-series gives an integral formal O_K-module by Lubin–Tate interpolation. The coefficient induction proves the law, action and unique strict same-parameter comparison. Strict means derivative one, and does not mean that the reduction of the coordinate map is the identity.

**Lubin–Tate series.** Fix a finite extension K/Q_p, O=O_K, residue field of size q, and uniformizer π. An admissible Lubin–Tate series f∈O[[X]] has constant coefficient zero, linear coefficient π and reduction X^q modulo (π). These are coefficient conditions, independent of a formal law. The standard example is πX+X^q.

**Lubin–Tate interpolation.** For admissible f,g for the same π and a finite list of coefficients a_i∈O, there is a unique integral multivariate series H with prescribed linear form Σa_i X_i and f∘H=H∘(g,…,g). Uniqueness also holds among series over K with that linear form. The construction is coefficientwise and commutes with isomorphisms of the input data.

**Lubin–Tate formal module.** For each admissible f construct F_f and [a]_f by interpolation with tangent forms X+Y and aX. Prove that F_f is a commutative formal O-module, [π]_f=f, and its special fiber has O-height one. A commutative formal law over O carrying an endomorphism with derivative π and reduction X^q is uniquely identified with this construction in its coordinate.

**Coordinate independence.** For admissible f,g for the same π, interpolation gives a unique strict O-linear isomorphism F_g→F_f; these isomorphisms compose transitively. They identify torsion schemes, Tate modules, characters and division fields. Over extensions of O they base change naturally. This does not assert that the isomorphism induces the identity on the special fiber.

stages.title: Torsion, Tate modules and the Artin comparison
stages.description:
Use pinned Weierstrass preparation and the parent’s actual p-divisible groups. Prove finite-height Tate freeness, then the rank-one division degrees and character isomorphism. Compare with the established arithmetic Artin map, including the inverse unit factor and the unramified twist on changing π.

**Finite-height torsion comparison.** Let G be a one-dimensional formal O_K-module over a complete noetherian local O_K-algebra R, with residue characteristic p and finite special-fiber O_K-height h. For m≥1, R[[X]]/([π^m]_G) is finite free of rank q^(hm) and its formal Hopf law defines a finite locally free group scheme. The levels are the π-power torsion of a connected p-divisible group in R07.1, whose p-height is h[K:Q_p]. Coefficient base change and coordinate isomorphisms identify these actual group schemes.

**Formal-module Tate module.** Over the integers of a finite extension L/K of characteristic zero, let G have O_K-height h. The π-adic inverse limit T_πG of geometric π-power torsion with transition [π] is free of rank h over O_K, and T_πG/π^m identifies with G[π^m](Lbar). The action of G_L is continuous and O_K-linear. Its underlying Z_p-module canonically identifies with the R07.1 Tate module of the associated p-divisible group, using the unit correction between π^e and p. The torsion module is (T_πG⊗K)/T_πG.

**Lubin–Tate division fields.** For F_f over O_K and m≥1, its primitive π^m-torsion consists of the O_K/π^m-module generators. For any generator t_m, K(t_m)=K(F_f[π^m]) is totally ramified of degree (q−1)q^(m−1). The action identifies its Galois group with (O_K/π^m)× and sends t_m to [a]t_m. Consecutive generators can be chosen with [π]t_(m+1)=t_m.

**Lubin–Tate character.** The actual G_K-action on the rank-one O_K-module T_πF defines a continuous character χ_π:G_K→O_K×, characterized by σ(t)=[χ_π(σ)]t at every torsion level. It factors through Gal(K(F[π∞])/K), where it is a topological isomorphism onto O_K×. The character is independent of a Tate basis and of the admissible π-series, with the isomorphisms specified in LT.1.

**Comparison with local reciprocity.** Use the ClassFieldTheory Layers 5–8 arithmetic local Artin map Art_K. For x=π^r u with u∈O_K×, χ_π(Art_K(x))=u^−1. In particular Art_K(π) fixes the Lubin–Tate torsion extension. Its finite level has norm subgroup π^Z(1+π^mO_K); the completed abelian reciprocity is the existing map. This theorem is a comparison, not a second construction of reciprocity.

**Change of uniformizer.** If π′=uπ with u∈O×, Lubin–Tate modules for π and π′ become isomorphic over the completed maximal unramified extension. Their G_K-characters have equal restriction to inertia, and χ_(π′)=χ_π·η_u, where η_u is the unramified character taking arithmetic Frobenius to u. The isomorphism has the Frobenius descent relation that accounts for this twist; it need not descend to O.

stages.title: Marked deformations at finite height
stages.description:
Use a specified complete local coefficient base and a marked residual formal module. Prove lifting, rigidity and the h−1-dimensional tangent computation, then construct the universal formal power-series base. Keep residue fields nonclosed and compare the height-two elliptic special case through the existing Serre–Tate theorem.

**Marked formal-module deformations.** Fix a field k with its O_K-residue action, a one-dimensional formal O_K-module G0/k of finite height h≥1, and a specified complete noetherian local O_K-algebra B with residue k. A deformation over a local Artinian B-algebra R with identified residue k is a formal O_K-module G/R together with an O_K-linear isomorphism G⊗k≃G0. Isomorphisms must commute with that marking. Extend the functor to complete noetherian local B-algebras by compatible Artinian quotients. No algebraic closure of k, nor canonical Cohen ring for an imperfect k, is implicit.

**Universal formal-module coefficients.** For O=O_K, construct the graded O-algebra representing one-dimensional commutative formal O-module laws with fixed tangent action in a coordinate. It is noncanonically a polynomial O-algebra on one generator in each positive weight. In weight q^j−1, a generator may be chosen from the X^(q^j) coefficient of [π]. This coefficient algebra constructs unrestricted lifts of a given residual law before imposing deformation equivalence.

**Formal-module deformation cocycles.** For a square-zero small extension R′→R with kernel I annihilated by m_R′ and a formal O_K-module G0/k, define the k-vector space of symmetric additive-law corrections Δ(X,Y) together with action corrections δ_a(X), satisfying the linearized associativity, additivity and multiplication identities and the fixed tangent action. Coordinate corrections ψ(X) with zero constant term define coboundaries; their linear coefficient need not vanish. H²_O(G0;I) is the quotient of these cocycles by those coboundaries.

**Lifting and rigidity.** For the marked deformation problem in LT.3 and every small Artinian extension R′→R, lifts exist. Once a starting lift is chosen, isomorphism classes of lifts form a torsor under H²_O(G0;ker(R′→R)). A homomorphism between finite-height formal O-modules over an Artinian base is determined by its reduction. In particular a marked isomorphism, when it exists, is unique. These statements pass to complete local bases by inverse limits.

**Finite-height tangent space.** For every residual formal O_K-module G0/k of finite height h≥1, H²_O(G0;k) has dimension h−1. After a compatible finite-jet normalization, the coefficients of X^(q^i) in δ_π, 1≤i<h, give a basis of its dual; every other correction is a coboundary modulo these classes. The dimension and the resulting tangent space are defined over k itself.

**Universal finite-height deformation.** For the specified B,k,G0 of LT.3, the marked deformation functor is represented on complete noetherian local B-algebras by a noncanonically chosen B[[t1,…,t_(h−1)]], with a universal formal O_K-module and marking. Pullback gives a bijection between continuous local B-algebra maps and marked deformation classes, natural in the base. For each pullback the marked comparison is unique. Residue-field and coefficient-base extensions have specified comparison maps; no canonical coordinates are claimed.

**Elliptic deformation compatibility.** For a supersingular elliptic curve E/k in the domain of the existing ModularCurves deformation and Serre–Tate theorems, completion at zero identifies its marked deformation functor with that of its connected height-two p-divisible group and then with the underlying formal Z_p-module deformation problem. The two universal one-parameter bases are isomorphic by this functor comparison. Formal logarithms and CM endomorphism actions commute with completion. A formal CM action on a lift is not asserted to arise from global elliptic CM.

stages.title: Unramified Honda and elliptic comparisons
stages.description:
Keep the Frobenius lift in Honda’s type operator explicit. Prove functional-equation integrality and the unramified converse, then derive the scalar-Frobenius comparison with corrected sign. The elliptic a_p=0 specialization gives parameter −p over W(F_p²), with its actual normalized logarithm and Tate maps.

**Honda logarithm types.** Let O be a complete characteristic-zero DVR with fraction field K, uniformizer π, and a specified prime power q and endomorphism σ of K preserving O and lifting the q-power residue map. Here q need not be the full residue-field size. For u=π+Σ_(i≥1)c_iT^i in the σ-skew series ring, define u⋆ℓ=πℓ(X)+Σc_iℓ^(σ^i)(X^(q^i)). A normalized rational logarithm has type u when u⋆ℓ∈πO[[X]]. The skew relation Ta=σ(a)T and the semilinear coefficient action are part of the definition; only finitely many terms contribute to each coefficient.

**Honda functional equation.** Under Honda’s condition (F) and the specified Frobenius lift, a normalized logarithm of special type u defines an integral commutative formal group ℓ^−1(ℓ(X)+ℓ(Y)). Logarithms of the same normalized type have integral strict comparison ℓ_2^−1ℓ_1. For source type u, target type v and tangent C∈O, the rational homomorphism is integral precisely when vC=t u for some t∈O_σ[[T]]. For the converse take O the integers of an unramified extension of Q_p, π=p, q=p and σ the p-Frobenius lift: every integral formal group then has a type, and the finite-height case admits a type of degree its height with unit final coefficient.

**Unramified Honda–Lubin–Tate comparison.** Let p≥5, O=W(F_p²), q=p², and s∈{1,−1}. For a one-dimensional commutative formal group G/O whose reduction has q-power Frobenius equal to [s p], its normalized logarithm has type p−sT² for the p-Frobenius lift. It is strictly isomorphic over O to the group with logarithm ℓ_s=Σ_(j≥0)(s p)^(-j)X^(q^j). The latter has an integral O-action and is a Lubin–Tate formal O-module for π=s p. The transported action on G is unique with its specified tangent embedding.

**Supersingular elliptic comparison.** For p≥5 and E/O with O=W(F_p²), if a_q(E)=2s p, s=±1, then q-Frobenius on the special elliptic curve is [s p], and the integral formal group of E is isomorphic to a Lubin–Tate formal O-module for s p. In particular, for E/Z_p with good reduction and a_p(E)=0, its base change to O has q-Frobenius [−p] and parameter −p. The comparison identifies formal logarithms, torsion and Tate modules with the transition-sign correction made explicit subsequent.

stages.title: Lattice kernels and integral quotient isogenies
stages.description:
Interpret an embedded Tate lattice as a finite flat kernel, construct the integral Serre-product quotient and retain its Frobenius-twisted marking. Classify homomorphisms within this isogeny class by lattice inclusion, prove setwise-stabilizer descent, and compare completed elliptic quotients.

**Tate lattices and finite kernels.** Let G be a finite-height formal O0-module over the integers of a finite extension of F0, with T=T_varpi0 G and V=T⊗F0. An O0-lattice L⊂V is a finite free spanning O0-submodule. For L⊃T define C_L=L/T inside V/T≃G[varpi0∞](F0bar). Its schematic closure in a sufficiently large finite torsion level is finite flat over any finite coefficient extension over which C_L is Galois stable. The field of setwise stability is distinguished from the field making all points rational.

**Integral lattice quotient isogenies.** For L⊃T as above, over the integers R of a finite extension where C_L is setwise stable, construct a formal O0-module G_L and an integral isogeny g_L:G→G_L with exactly that finite flat kernel. In a splitting extension use the normalized Serre product g_L(X)=∏_(c∈C_L)(X−_G c). If #C_L=q0^N then its reduction is X^(q0^N), and G_L reduces to the q0^N-Frobenius twist of G0. The product is a series, rather than an assumed polynomial in X.

**Homomorphisms in the lattice isogeny class.** For quotient objects of a fixed G, conjugation by g_L identifies Hom_O0(G_L1,G_L2) with {a∈End_O0(G)⊗F0 : aL1⊂L2}. This assertion concerns the known isogeny class. In particular End(G_L) is its multiplier ring. Isomorphisms correspond to aL1=L2. The identification commutes with composition, scalar action and coefficient extension in the domain of the given homomorphisms.

**Descent of lattice quotients.** For a quotient of a coefficient-defined formal module G, the normalized product and quotient descend to the fixed field of the setwise Galois stabilizer of C_L, equivalently L. Under arithmetic Artin in the CM Lubin–Tate case the lattice transforms by a^−1. Descent of the quotient together with its normalized isogeny follows from this stability. Minimality for the marked quotient alone is a separate theorem in LT.6.

**Elliptic quotient compatibility.** If G is the formal completion of an elliptic curve and C_L is the completion of a finite flat elliptic subgroup supported at the zero special-fiber point, the completion of the existing elliptic quotient is canonically isomorphic to G_L. The completed elliptic isogeny and g_L differ only by this specified integral target coordinate. The induced torsion, Tate and logarithm maps agree.

stages.title: Canonical and Frobenius-marked quasi-canonical lifts
stages.description:
Construct the height-one CM lift over the CM coefficient ring. Its lattice quotients are marked quasi-canonical lifts. Classify both marked and unmarked objects, identify their multiplier orders, and prove the smallest field containing the CM field by the marked Artin stabilizer. Quadratic orders have a separate conductor-level classification.

**Canonical CM lift.** Let F/F0 be a finite extension, O_F its integers, π_F a uniformizer and k_F its residue field. The standard Lubin–Tate O_F-module H with [π_F]=π_F X+X^(#k_F), restricted to O0, is the canonical CM lift of its own special fiber with its designated O_F-action and tangent embedding. Its underlying O0-height is [F:F0]. For a chosen isomorphism of a residual formal O_F-module with this special fiber, transport the marking; over a complete unramified coefficient extension with the specified residue embedding, it is the unique marked lift of that O_F-module.

**Frobenius-marked quasi-canonical lifts.** For canonical H and an O0-lattice L in V=T⊗F0≃F containing T, define H_L by the integral quotient construction, with its Frobenius marking to Hbar^(q0^N) when [L:T]=q0^N. Extend to arbitrary lattices by multiplying by a sufficiently negative power of π_F and compare the resulting markings through [π_F]bar=X^(#k_F). Thus the invariant is a π_F^Z-lattice class with its specified Frobenius-twist component. Its endomorphism order is O_L={a∈F:aL⊂L}, containing O0. A quasi-canonical lift of level s in the quadratic case will mean O_L=O0+varpi0^s O_F.

**Marked and unmarked lattice classification.** For quasi-canonical H_L, unmarked O0-linear isomorphism classes correspond to F×-homothety classes of O0-lattices, equivalently O_F×-orbits of π_F^Z-lattice classes. Within a common coherently specified Frobenius-twist component, marked isomorphism holds exactly when the π_F^Z-lattice classes coincide. More generally the unmarked class is determined by its order O_L and the proper O_L-lattice class; equality of orders alone need not suffice outside the quadratic case.

**Quadratic CM orders.** For a quadratic local-field extension F/F0, with O0-uniformizer varpi0, define O_s=O0+varpi0^s O_F for s≥0. Every O0-order in O_F is exactly one O_s. The conductor in O_F is varpi0^s O_F, with O_0=O_F distinguished. If s≥1, O_s×=O0×(1+varpi0^s O_F). This uses the smaller-field uniformizer in both the ramified and unramified cases.

**Quadratic level classification.** For quadratic F/F0, every proper O_s-lattice in F is free of rank one over O_s. Consequently there is exactly one unmarked quasi-canonical O0-module isomorphism class of each level s. Its marked classes form a simply transitive O_F×/O_s×-set in each compatible Frobenius component. A standard representative is L_s=varpi0^−s O0·t+T for a primitive element t of the rank-one O_F Tate module T; it has multiplier order O_s.

**Smallest marked field of definition.** For a quasi-canonical H_L over its finite residue coefficient field k_F and a fixed universal deformation coordinate over B=O_(F^ur), where F^ur/F0 is the maximal unramified subextension of F/F0, let m_L denote its marked modulus (an (n−1)-tuple for n=[F:F0]). The smallest field containing F over which this marked deformation is defined is M_L=F(m_L). Under the existing arithmetic local reciprocity it is the class field of π_F^Z O_L×⊂F×. This statement is over the nonclosed residue field; after completed unramified base change it gives the usual Gross formulation. It does not assert absolute minimality among fields not containing F.

stages.title: Quadratic orders, minimal fields and boundary tests
stages.description:
Compute quadratic marked field degrees for unramified and ramified CM extensions and prove that the positive-level deformation modulus is a uniformizer. Specialize to the BKO primed tower, retain its tame factor, give the ramified Honda counterexample and compute the neighboring conductor lattices.

**Quadratic ring-class degrees.** Let F/F0 be quadratic, q0=#k0, π_F fixed and s≥1. The marked level-s field M_s/F is totally ramified, has Artin subgroup π_F^Z O_s×, and Gal(M_s/F)≃O_F×/O_s×≃(O_F/varpi0^sO_F)×/(O0/varpi0^sO0)×. Its degree is q0^(s−1)(q0+1) when F/F0 is unramified and q0^s when it is ramified. The canonical level-zero field is M_0=F of degree one, separately. These include ramification above 2.

**Quadratic deformation moduli.** In the quadratic situation, use B equal to the integers of the maximal unramified subextension of F/F0 and a universal height-two formal O0-deformation over B[[t]]. For every level-s quasi-canonical lift with s≥1, its marked modulus t_s is a uniformizer of M_s. With v_F(π_F)=1, v_F(t_s)=1/[M_s:F], hence 1/(q0^(s−1)(q0+1)) in the unramified case and 1/q0^s in the ramified case. This is a statement about a valid universal deformation parameter over B, with its specified marking, not an arbitrary analytic function on the deformation space.

**BKO quasi-canonical fields.** Fix p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, O=O_Φ, π=−p, κ=χ_π and canonical H. For a primitive t∈T_πH and s≥1, let L_s=p^−s Z_p t+T, H_s=H_(L_s), O_s=Z_p+p^sO and Ψ′_s the smallest field containing Φ of its marked modulus. Then Ψ′_s is the fixed field of κ^−1(O_s×), equivalently the Artin class field of (−p)^Z Z_p×(1+p^sO). It has degree p^(s−1)(p+1), and H_s has exactly endomorphism order O_s. Set Ψ′_0=Φ only as a separate canonical-level convention.

**Infinite primed ring-class tower.** For Ψ′_∞=⋃_(s≥1)Ψ′_s in the BKO setup, κ induces Gal(Ψ′_∞/Φ)≃O×/Z_p×. Teichmüller and deep-unit logarithm identify this topological group with μ_(p+1)×Z_p, hence Z/(p+1)×Z_p after a choice of tame generator and a Z_p-basis of the negative line. The finite tame factor is canonical as the prime-to-p torsion subgroup. Its fixed field will be the anticyclotomic pro-p tower of LT.8.

**Ramified Honda boundary test.** The unramified hypothesis in LT.4 cannot be discarded: the level-one BKO quasi-canonical quotient H_1 over O_(Ψ′_1) has special-fiber q-Frobenius [−p] and height two, but its geometric integral Z_p-endomorphism ring is Z_p+pO, not O. It is therefore not isomorphic over any finite coefficient extension to an O-Lubin–Tate formal module. Its coefficient ring is totally ramified of degree p+1 over O, where −p is no longer a uniformizer.

**Neighboring level lattices.** In the BKO unramified quadratic isogeny class, the p+1 index-p superlattices of a rank-two Z_p-lattice give the neighboring quotient isogenies. At level s≥1, one neighbor has level s−1 up to F×-homothety and p have level s+1; at level zero all p+1 have level one. The level-s stabilizer acts transitively on the outward p neighbors, and the canonical-level tame quotient acts transitively on the first p+1 neighbors. This provides isogeny inputs for subsequent trace recurrences without claiming those recurrences here.

stages.title: The BKO tame and anticyclotomic towers
stages.description:
In the unramified quadratic p≥5, π=−p setting, construct κ, Δ, ω and the two principal-unit eigendirections. Define the actual Θ_n and Ψ_n fields, compare their fixed subgroups with Ψ′_s, and make the torsion-generator, modulus-generator and alternating π/p Tate-generator formulas explicit.

**BKO tame character data.** In the p≥5, Φ/Q_p unramified quadratic, π=−p setup, define Φ_n=Φ(H[π^(n+1)]) for n≥0, Φ_−1=Φ and Φ_∞=⋃Φ_n. Restrict the actual Tate character to obtain κ:Gal(Φ_∞/Φ)≃O×. Define Δ as κ^−1(μ_(p²−1)) and Γ=κ^−1(1+pO); the restriction Δ→Gal(Φ_0/Φ) is an isomorphism and Gal(Φ_∞/Φ)=Δ×Γ canonically. Define ω=κ|Δ, the Teichmüller character with values in O×.

**Cyclotomic and anticyclotomic directions.** Let c be the nontrivial automorphism of Φ/Q_p. Conjugation acts on κ-values by c, and preserves Γ. Under the imported log:1+pO≃pO, define G+ and G− from the images of (1+c)/2 and (1−c)/2. Then Γ=G+×G−, κ(G+)=1+pZ_p and κ(G−)={u∈1+pO:N_(Φ/Q_p)(u)=1}; each is topologically free rank one over Z_p. The factors are canonical, while isomorphisms with the additive group Z_p require a basis of the corresponding line.

**BKO finite fixed fields.** For n≥0 define Θ_n=Φ_n^Δ and Ψ_n=Θ_n^(image G+), using restriction of the infinite Galois subgroups. Then [Θ_n:Φ]=p^(2n), [Ψ_n:Φ]=p^n, Θ_0=Ψ_0=Φ, and the transition inclusions are the ones induced from Φ_n. At infinity Θ_∞=Φ_∞^Δ and Ψ_∞=Φ_∞^(ΔG+), with Gal(Ψ_∞/Φ) identified with G−. The extension Ψ_∞/Q_p is Galois with inversion action of c; its maximal dihedral pro-p assertion refers to its subgroup over Φ, since its full Q_p-Galois group contains C2.

**Field and generator comparisons.** For primitive compatible π^(n+1)-division points v_n, Φ_n=Φ(v_n), and replacing the Tate generator does not change Φ_n, Θ_n or Ψ_n. Let Δ′=Δ/μ_(p−1), the tame subgroup of Gal(Ψ′_∞/Φ) of order p+1. For n≥0, Ψ_n=(Ψ′_(n+1))^Δ′; at infinity (Ψ′_∞)^Δ′=Ψ_∞. For s≥1, Ψ′_s∩Ψ_s=Ψ_(s−1), Ψ′_s Ψ_s=Ψ′_(s+1), and restriction identifies Gal(Ψ′_(s+1)/Ψ′_s) with Gal(Ψ_s/Ψ_(s−1)). A universal marked modulus t_s generates Ψ′_s over Φ. These generator statements retain the specified separable closure and embeddings.

**π-adic and p-adic generators.** For a Tate generator (v_n)_(n≥0) with [−p]v_(n+1)=v_n and v_n of order p^(n+1), define w_n=[(−1)^n]v_n. Then [p]w_(n+1)=w_n and (w_n) is the corresponding p-adic Tate generator. This map is O-linear, Galois equivariant and invertible, and preserves every finite division field. Under an elliptic formal isomorphism Ehat≃H it gives the R07.1 p-adic Tate-module comparison with the initial-component normalization w_0=v_0. At a fixed index n, logarithm and finite formal trace commute with the scalar j_n=[(−1)^n] when the same scalar is used on both ends. If source and target are assigned indices n,m instead, Tr∘j_n=[(−1)^(n+m)]∘j_m∘Tr. The alternation is not silently commuted across a field trace between different indices.

stages.title: Formal traces and compatible tower maps
stages.description:
Construct finite additive formal traces. The tame trace from Ψ′_(s+1) to Ψ_s is surjective and commutes with the p-step traces, logarithms and elliptic coordinates. These proved maps export the common local foundation while the consumers retain their cohomological, diamond, Coleman and distinguished-point constructions.

**Finite formal traces.** For a formal O0-module G over O_K and a finite Galois extension L/K, define Tr^G_(L/K):G(m_L)→G(m_K) by the finite formal sum of σx over Gal(L/K). More generally the same formula on embeddings gives the finite separable trace. It is O0-linear, natural for coefficient-defined formal homomorphisms, compatible with towers, coefficient field isomorphisms and coordinate transport. Its value is invariant and lies in m_K; logarithms carry it to the usual field trace.

**Tame descent on formal points.** For s≥0 in the BKO setup, define D_s=Tr^H_(Ψ′_(s+1)/Ψ_s):H(m_(Ψ′_(s+1)))→H(m_(Ψ_s)), a formal sum over Δ′ of order p+1. This uses Ψ_s=(Ψ′_(s+1))^Δ′. It is O-linear, compatible with coordinate transport and the elliptic formal comparison, and independent of any enumerated tame generator. On a point already over Ψ_s it is [p+1]_H, whose inverse exists integrally, so D_s is surjective.

**Trace-compatible tower comparisons.** For s≥0 and x∈H(m_(Ψ′_(s+2))), the BKO field rectangle gives Tr^H_(Ψ_(s+1)/Ψ_s)(D_(s+1)x)=D_s(Tr^H_(Ψ′_(s+2)/Ψ′_(s+1))x). The same square commutes after normalized logarithm and after a coefficient-defined elliptic formal isomorphism. The π/p Tate systems have the compatible transition comparison of LT.8; if alternating sign coordinates are assigned to different field levels, their formal traces carry exactly the correction in that node. Consequently D sends any primed trace-compatible point system to an unprimed trace-compatible system. The formal O_K-module, torsion and finite-height deformation APIs export to the existing two-tower and diamond consumers without importing their classifications.
